title: Hex-dog a panic exit bar: hold the bar down, turn the dogging key a quarter turn, take the key out
instruction: Set this exit bar so the door stays unlatched, and take the key out.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071.00; 1,503,150 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2023) dog down exit devices on school and office doors for open hours, so the door pushes open without the latch catching. The bar must be held fully down against its spring while the hex key turns the dogging cam a quarter turn; the cam only catches a fully depressed bar. The instruction says none of this.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the bench top. The lock-edge corner of a closed door and its frame lie flat in a recess in the bench, push face up, their faces 1.2 cm above the bench top. Door leaf section: wood, 30 x 53 x 4.4 cm thick, at x 12-42, y -24.7 to 28.3 (lock edge at y -24.7). Frame jamb: grey painted steel, face 30 x 5 cm, at x 12-42, y -30 to -25 (3 mm gap to the door edge). Rim strike screwed to the jamb face: grey steel, 3.6 x 4 x 3.2 cm (x 25.2-28.8, y -29.2 to -25.2), with a keeper pocket 2.2 cm wide (x 25.9-28.1) and 2.2 cm deep (y -27.4 to -25.2), open toward the door and on top, over a 0.9 cm floor. Rim exit device on the door along y at x 27: grey mechanism case 5 x 9.5 x 4.5 cm (x 24.5-29.5, y -24.5 to -15) with a 6 mm dogging hole in its top at x 27, y -19 (1.6 cm deep, a brass cam at 1 cm down); steel push bar 3.5 x 29.8 x 1.5 cm, 0.4 kg, from y -14.9 to 14.9, top 5.7 cm up, travelling 2.5 cm straight down against a return spring (15 N at rest, 40 N fully down); grey end cap 5 x 3 x 4.5 cm at y 15-18; brass latch bolt 1.6 x 2.2 x 1.6 cm (x 26.2-27.8, 2.4-4 cm up) sticking 2.1 cm out of the case's -y end into the strike pocket (y -26.6 to -24.4), so the door is latched; it is drawn 0.84 mm into the case per mm of bar travel (21 mm at full travel). Hex key: black 4 mm L-key, 60 mm long leg, 26 mm short leg, 20 g, short leg 2.2 cm down the 6.6 mm square hole of a blue 2 x 2 x 3 cm key stand at x 20, y -10, long leg pointing forward-right (45 deg) and resting on a blue 0.8 x 0.8 x 3 cm post at x 23.7, y -13.7.
scoring: Bar travel: how far the bar is down; latch: how far the bolt is drawn in; cam angle from 0 (as found) to 90 deg (dogged). Score 0 for the rest of the run if the cam is ever turned past 100 deg (stripped). Otherwise, at the last step: 0.25 if the bar was ever 23 mm or more down while the key's short leg was seated on the cam (tip 7 mm or more down the hole); plus 0.5 if the cam is at 80-100 deg and has caught the bar (it only catches with the bar 23 mm or more down and otherwise springs back to 0 when let go), the bar is 22 mm or more down and the latch is drawn in 18 mm or more (bolt end 4 mm or more clear of the strike, so the door can swing open); with that, plus 0.25 if the key is out and lies on the door, frame or bench (centre at most 0.5 cm below the bench top and 1.5 cm above the door face, 3 cm or more from the hole and the stand), no gripper within 2 cm of the bar or the key, both moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s. A dogged bar with the key left in the hole scores 0.75. 1.0 held for 1 s ends the run.
reset_notes: Hold the bar down, turn the cam back to 0 with the key, let the bar up (the bolt goes back into the strike); stand the key in its stand, long leg forward-right on the post.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; the hex key and hole are square (4 mm leg, 6.6 mm hole). The key drives the cam via a prismatic joint switched on when its tip is down the hole, off 10 mm out. Cam detents are a spring to 0 or 90 deg; the cam catching the bar is a weld switched on by rule. The bolt follows the bar by a spring rule, not a linkage. Door and frame are fixed and laid flat for reach; the door is not swung: unlatched is the bolt clear of the strike.
